meta.title: Captionshaper: free offline auto subtitles for Mac and Windows
meta.desc: Drop in a video and get accurate, word-timed captions in seconds. Export SRT, VTT or burn in TikTok-style captions. Free, open source, and nothing is uploaded.

hero.h1: Captions that keep up with you.
hero.sub: Drop in a video. Captionshaper writes every word with its timing, right on your computer. Fix anything, pick a style, export. Nothing is uploaded.
hero.note: macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon · Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit)

live.p: Captionshaper finds the speech, skips the music and silence, and the words appear as they're written. A one-minute clip takes about ten seconds on an M-series Mac.

feat.h: Good captions, not just a transcript.
items: Nothing over music
Voice detection finds where people speak. Intros, music and silence stay clean, so no made-up words.
Timed to the word
Each word starts when the voice does, for captions that feel in sync and word-by-word highlights that land.
Lines that read well
Breaks fall at sentence and clause ends, never after “the” or “to”, and never across a long pause.
Made for vertical video
Pop and word-by-word styles, plus a phone view that shows where TikTok, Reels and Shorts put their buttons.
Fix it fast
Uncertain words are underlined. Edit in place, find and replace, split, merge, undo. Your edits are saved.
Every format
SRT, VTT, ASS and plain text, or an MP4 with captions burned in, ready to post.

styles.h: Pick a look. See it exactly as it exports.
styles.p: Nine looks to start from, including Bold, Highlight box, One word, Reveal and Neon, with eleven caption fonts. The spoken word can change colour or sit on a box, and words can pop, fade or slide in. The preview is the finished video: same fonts, sizes and timing.

priv.h: Your videos never leave your computer.
priv.p: No account, no upload, no watermark, no limits. The only download is the speech model, once. After that Captionshaper works without the internet.
items: Speech recognition runs on your Mac or PC
No account and no tracking
Open source under the GPL
Is it really free?
Yes. No trial, no watermark, no limits. Captionshaper is open source, and you can support it on Ko-fi if it saves you time.
Does it upload my video?
No. Everything happens on your computer. The app downloads the speech model once (about 570 MB), and that's its only connection to the internet.
Which languages does it understand?

About 99, including English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese and Japanese. It detects the language for you. For less common languages, the Most accurate model makes fewer mistakes.
How accurate is it?

On clear speech it gets almost every word right. We test it on clips with known scripts in English, Spanish and German: 0.7% word error rate, with captions within 0.15 seconds of the voice. Noisy audio and strong accents make more mistakes, which is why fixing words is quick.
Can it translate?
It can turn speech in any supported language into English captions. Tick “Translate to English” before you start.
Is it fast on Windows?
It runs on the processor, about one to two times real time on a recent PC. On Apple Silicon Macs it uses the GPU and is around five times faster than real time.
Does it work on Intel Macs?
Not yet. The Mac version needs Apple Silicon (M1 or newer).

dl.title: Download Captionshaper
dl.sub: Free, for Mac and Windows. Version {v}.
dl.macReq: Apple Silicon (M1 or newer), macOS 12 or later
macSteps: Open the .dmg and drag Captionshaper to Applications.
Right-click Captionshaper and choose Open, then click Open.
If macOS still blocks it, go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click Open Anyway.
winSteps: Run the installer. If SmartScreen appears, click More info, then Run anyway.
Windows may ask to install the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime. Say yes; the speech engine needs it.
dl.why: Captionshaper isn't signed with a paid Apple or Microsoft certificate yet, so both systems ask once.
dl.src: Source code and older versions on GitHub

privacyPage.title: Privacy
body: Captionshaper runs on your computer. Your videos, audio, captions and edits stay there.
The app makes one kind of network request: downloading a speech model from Hugging Face (huggingface.co) when you click Download. That request doesn't include anything about your files.
There are no accounts, no analytics and no tracking in the app.
This website is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may keep standard server logs; see GitHub's privacy statement. The site itself has no cookies or analytics.

footer.tagline: Free, offline auto-subtitles for Mac and Windows.

featuresPage.title: Features
featuresPage.lead: From the first word it hears to the finished video, all on your own computer.

sections.p: Speech recognition runs on your Mac or PC with OpenAI's Whisper model, so it understands accents, fast talkers and around 99 languages.
items: Finds the speech first
Voice detection skips intros, music and silence, so no words get invented over a beat drop.
Timed to the word
Each word starts when the voice does. Captions appear in sync, and word highlights land on the beat.
Detects the language
Or pick it yourself. It can also turn any supported language into English captions.
Three models
Recommended for most videos, Most accurate for harder languages and audio, Fast for quick drafts.

sections.p: A transcript isn't captions. Captionshaper decides where every caption starts and ends, and where each line breaks.
items: Natural line breaks
Breaks fall at sentence and clause ends, never after “the”, “a” or “to”.
Never across a pause
When the speaker stops, the caption stops. Lines fit the width of your video.
Easy to fix
Words it isn't sure about are underlined. Edit in place, find and replace, split, merge and undo.
Saved as you go
Close the app and open the same video later: your edits are still there.

sections.p: Nine looks to start from and eleven caption fonts. The preview is exactly what gets exported.
items: Highlight the spoken word
Change its colour or put it on a box, the way the big creators do.
Word animations
Pop, fade in or slide up. Hide or dim the words that haven't been said yet.
Outline, shadow and glow
Each with its own colour, plus a background box behind lines.
Phone view
See where TikTok, Reels and Shorts put their buttons, so captions never hide under them.

sections.p: Take your captions wherever they need to go.
items: Video with captions
An MP4 with the captions burned in, ready to post.
Subtitle files
SRT for YouTube and video editors, VTT for the web, ASS with your full style.
Transcript
Plain text, split into paragraphs at long pauses.
Private by design
Nothing is uploaded. After the one-time model download, it works offline.

faqPage.title: FAQ
more: An MP4 video with the captions burned in, SRT subtitles (YouTube, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut), VTT for websites, ASS with your full style, and a plain-text transcript.
Yes. Click any caption to edit it, use find and replace, split or merge captions, and undo anything. Words Captionshaper isn't sure about are underlined so you can check them first.
Does it work for TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts?
Yes. The Bold, Highlight, One word and Reveal styles are made for vertical video, and the phone view shows where each app puts its buttons so your captions stay clear of them.
Most video and audio files: MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, MP3, WAV, M4A and more, including iPhone videos.
How long can a video be?
There's no limit. A 10-minute video takes about two minutes on an Apple Silicon Mac. Longer videos simply take longer.
Why does my computer warn me when I first open it?
Captionshaper isn't signed with a paid Apple or Microsoft certificate yet, so both systems ask once. The download page shows how to open it, and you can check the file's checksum there.

about.title: About
about.lead: I'm Elvis Zygmanta. Hollowbit is my studio for small, free tools that do one job well and treat the people using them with respect.
why: Captions are no longer optional. Most people watch short videos with the sound off, and a video without captions gets scrolled past.
The usual tools upload your video to a server, put the best styles behind a subscription and add a watermark until you pay. For something a normal computer can do in a minute, that felt wrong.
Captionshaper does it on your own computer, for free: accurate captions, styles that look like the ones you see every day, and nothing uploaded.
rules: Not in the app, not on the website.
You shouldn't need to sign up to caption a video.
No analytics and no data collection.
Every line of code is public.
tech: OpenAI's speech model, run locally with whisper.cpp
Token timestamps matched to the voice
Burns the captions into the video
One app for Mac and Windows
Automated tests drive the real app and measure accuracy

support.title: Support
support.help_p: Found a bug or something not working? Open an issue on GitHub. Say which computer you're on, which version of Captionshaper, and what you tried.
support.give_p: Captionshaper is free and stays free. A tip helps pay for the code-signing certificates that make the security warnings go away.

privacyFull.short: Captionshaper runs on your computer. Your videos, audio and captions never leave it.
sections: What the app does with your files

Captionshaper reads the video or audio you open, recognises the speech and writes captions, all on your computer. It saves your edits in its own folder so you can come back to them. Nothing is sent anywhere.

The app makes one kind of request: downloading a speech model from Hugging Face (huggingface.co) when you click Download. That request contains nothing about your files. After that, Captionshaper works with the internet off.
There are none, in the app or on this website.

This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may keep standard server logs, as described in GitHub's privacy statement. The site sets no cookies. Your chosen language is remembered in your own browser only.
Questions about privacy? Open an issue on GitHub.
